stem.text: Let \( s = h(u) \) be a twice-differentiable function. Suppose that \( h''(1) = 11 \). Write this statement in Leibniz notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( \left. \frac{d^{2}s}{du^{2}} \right|_{u=1} = 11 \), so the rate of change, with respect to u, of the rate of change of s when u = 1 is 11.

worked_solution.text: In \( h''(1) \) the function is h, the independent variable is u, and the second derivative is evaluated at u = 1, so the statement is about one input only.
In Leibniz notation the same statement is \( \left. \frac{d^{2}s}{du^{2}} \right|_{u=1} = 11 \).
It says that the rate of change, with respect to u, of the rate of change of s when u = 1 is 11.

options.label: \( \frac{d^{2}s}{du^{2}} = 11 \), so the rate of change, with respect to u, of the rate of change of s, the same at every u, is 11.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the second derivative function

options.label: \( \left(\frac{ds}{du}\right)^{2} = 11 \text{ at } u = 1 \), so the square of the rate of change of s with respect to u when u = 1 is 11.
options.derivation: the second derivative written as the square of the first derivative

options.label: \( \left. \frac{d^{2}s}{du^{2}} \right|_{u=1} = 11 \), so the rate of change, with respect to u, of the rate of change of s when u = 1 is 11.
\( \left. \frac{d^{2}u}{ds^{2}} \right|_{u=1} = 11 \), so the rate of change, with respect to s, of the rate of change of u when u = 1 is 11.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable
